text:
Maya: quick sync — I sketched a minimal 'smoke prober' contract we can ship into the intake path. want feedback on boundaries before I write the rfc.
Raj: nice. can you paste the contract sketch here?
Maya: sure — thinking of 3 calls: `register_model(metadata)`, `request_probe(model_id, probe_spec) -> probe_id`, `probe_status(probe_id)`. probe runs asynchronously and writes a small result blob.
Lin: what does `probe_spec` contain? sampling policy? golden inputs? latency targets?
Maya: proto: `probe_spec = {samples: int, seed: int, inputs: ref_to_golden_set?, metrics: [latency,p99,token_err_rate], target_slo: ms, allow_fallback: bool}`
Sam: +1 for keeping it tiny. question: where do golden sets live? in model registry or bench storage?
Maya: prefer model registry link (immutable artifact id). bench can pull from registry or local cache. avoids duplicating golden artifacts.
Zoe: how do we handle quantized vs fp32 binaries? some probes fail weirdly due to quantization nondeterminism.
Raj: we should add `binary_profile` in metadata and have probe shim map compatible runner. if incompatible, probe should return `compatibility: false` with reason codes.
Lin: compatibility reasons should be machine-readable so automation can decide: `fallback_to_variant`, `require_rebuild`, `reject`.
Maya: Agreed. Also: probes must be cheap. default samples=16, run on low-priority pool and timeout=5s per sample.
Sam: need an escape hatch for heavyweight smoke (e.g., 200 samples) for suspicious models. maybe `priority: low|high` in `probe_spec`.
Maya: added `priority`. low runs on smoke pool, high schedules bench run.
OpsBot: reminder: smoke-pool currently has quota 200 concurrent jobs. Please include rate limits in spec.
Zoe: how about result schema? minimal: `{ok:bool, compat:bool, metrics:{latency:p50,p90,p99}, diffs:[{input_id,score_delta}], artifacts:[trace_id]}`
Raj: include `golden_checksum` and `model_fingerprint` in the result for auditability.
Lin: we should also capture KV-cache warmup behaviour. probes often miss perf regressions when warmup differs in prod.
Maya: suggestion: add a boolean `include_kv_warmup` default false. when true, run a short prefix sequence to populate cache.
Sam: rollout policy note — probe failures map to different flows: soft-fail (warn), block intake, or auto-rollback. need mapping table.
Maya: propose default mapping: `compat=false` -> block intake; `metric_regression <10%` -> warn and canary; `metric_regression >10%` -> block. config override per team.
Zoe: can we tie regressions to evaluation prompts rather than aggregate token-level diffs? a small eval-suite in registry could be referenced.
Maya: yes — add `eval_suite_id` to `probe_spec`. results should include per-eval-case diffs so we can alert on functionally significant regressions.
Raj: implementation note — `probe_status` should expose `state: queued|running|done|errored` and `retry_count`.
Lin: error modes: transient infra error (retry), model crash (reject), mismatch in signature (block). need clear labels.
Maya: I'll draft the RFC with these shape points and include a small example payload and state machine. action items:
Maya: 1) I'll write the short RFC by EOD Friday with examples.
Sam: 2) I'll prototype a smoke-runner shim that interprets `probe_spec` and emits the result schema — can do next week.
Zoe: 3) I'll enumerate the common regressions and map to human-friendly alerts.
Raj: Can we also log probe traces to the console with `trace_id` so SRE can reproduce? prefer trace retention 30d.
Maya: agreed on 30d for probe traces.
OpsBot: note: feature-flag gating will be required. please add `feature_flag: onboard_smoke_prober_v1` to rollout plan.
Lin: small UX ask — include a `quick_preview` boolean that returns a lightweight summary synchronously for UI immediacy.
Maya: ok add `quick_preview` with tight time budget (200ms) that returns only pass/fail + small metric.
Sam: :thumbsup: sounds good. excited to see the RFC.
Maya: thanks all — will post the RFC link here when ready.
Raj: ping me when it's up, I'll review the compatibility reason codes.
Zoe: I'll prepare the eval-suite examples.
Maya: end.
